title: The Green Knight - a game/experience we're developing built on 3js and claudecode
author: Studiograylake
selftext:
Play at: [https://erhanofgraylake.itch.io/the-green-knight](https://erhanofgraylake.itch.io/the-green-knight)

Headphones recommended. 

Studio website: [studiograylake.com](http://studiograylake.com)

What it is:

The Green Knight is inspired by the late 14th-century *Sir Gawain and the Green Knight* Arthurian poem. 

It is a walk in the woods.

We tried to make the experience as comprehensive as possible, with all animations procedural, including the characters motion with 0 key frame work. The wind affects the weather, the rain, the trees, the grass, and the knight's plume. Terrain influences how the character moves and water is fully refractive and reflective. Climbing down a hill makes more armor sounds, birds go quiet when it rains, the wind whooshes and trees rustle in a fully 3D stereo soundscape experience. 

It comes with a terrain generator and a set of workshop tools where you can adjust and change a ton of parameters to try your own settings. 

\* working on: The motion responsiveness, more stances and actions, various armor and plumes, cloth, flag, banner, and tabards, better clouds that cast real shadows, better terrain generator and biome aware flora placement, and *many many others planned,* along with a narrative edge which looks at the poem from a different perspective.  

We've used claude code for almost every bit, created a development pipeline that focuses on the design and framework first, developed it across several weeks of work, tuning and adjusting every bit along the way. We worked pretty hard to avoid detailed AI style "final" work aesthetics and design, so I personally consider it hand-made rather than "prompted into existence" (not that it reduces from the experience, but let's be honest, AI created work are not exactly known for their scalability yet)

How we used claude code: We've separated our approach to various Leads that take on focused Labs. The whole thing is connected via MCP to a project management tool we've developed called nargraph that acts as a memory and context tuning tool as well as balancing the work between various sessions. This allowed us to make the project relatively scalable, and organize the work between the two developers of our studio.
